# Lucem — GPU Image Analysis for Histology & Microscopy

> Lucem is a Rust + Python + WebAssembly platform for viewing gigapixel OME-Zarr / OME-TIFF slides, building live GPU processing pipelines (CubeCL), running CUDA ML cell segmentation (StarDist, InstanSeg), writing `@lucem.op` scripts, and composing publication figures.

## Quick links

- Docs home: https://neuro-kitchen.github.io/lucem/
- Interactive browser viewer: https://neuro-kitchen.github.io/lucem/viewer/
- Repository: https://github.com/neuro-kitchen/lucem

## Installation

- Python (core): `pip install lucem`
- Python + browser app: `pip install "lucem[web]"` then `lucem web`
- Rust CLI & Desktop app: `cargo run -p lucem-app` / `cargo build -p lucem-cli`

## Workspaces (App)

- **Explore (`Ctrl+1`)**: Multi-channel pyramid viewer, Multiview split, annotations, edge-snapping Magic Wand (`W`, `Alt` to erase), Pixel Probe HUD (`I`), Histology recipes.
- **Pipeline (`Ctrl+2`)**: Non-destructive GPU node graph (52 CubeCL ops), live node previews, Script & Model nodes, `.lucem-recipe.json` export.
- **Analyze (`Ctrl+3`)**: Measurement tables (Polars on desktop, Region LOD summaries in browser).
- **Code (`Ctrl+4`)**: Built-in Python & Rust `@lucem.op` editor with LSP completion/hover and Astral `ruff` diagnostics.
- **Figure (`Ctrl+5`)**: Multi-panel publication composer with channel/stage presets, ROI crop sync, calibrated scale bars, and PNG / SVG export.

## Core Python API

- `lucem.open(path)` — open OME-Zarr, OME-TIFF, or standard image as a lazy `Pyramid`
- `@lucem.op(family="Filter", halo=12)` — register a custom tiled NumPy/SciPy operation with auto-generated UI parameters
- `lucem.ops.*` — 52 GPU-accelerated filtering, morphology, threshold, and segmentation operations
- `lucem.hist.*` — tissue detection, cell detection (threshold, StarDist, InstanSeg), stain separation, intensity scoring
- `lucem.web.serve(...)` — launch the browser viewer locally
